array.name: share_card_quotes
array.item: Every cloud has a silver lining.
After rain comes sunshine.
No rain, no flowers.
The sun always shines above the clouds.
A smooth sea never made a skilled sailor.
Storms make trees take deeper roots.
The greater the storm, the brighter the rainbow.
Wherever you go, no matter the weather, bring your own sunshine.
Rain is just confetti from the sky.
Let the wind rearrange your thoughts.
Cloudy days make you appreciate the sun.
Soft rain grows quiet courage.
Blue sky days are for deep breaths.
Snow turns noise into hush.
Fog asks you to walk a little slower.
Thunder is only weather clearing its throat.
Sunrise is proof that endings can glow.
Sunset is the sky signing off kindly.
Pack patience with your umbrella.
Wear kindness; it works in every climate.
A warm drink fixes more than cold hands.
Look up: the sky is still doing its best.
Weather changes. So can your mood—for the better.
Take the long way when the light is good.
Leave room in your day for a breeze.
If it’s raining, practice soft steps.
If it’s windy, hold your hat and your hope.
If it’s hot, water yourself like a plant.
If it’s cold, share your warmth.
May your winters be warm and your springs gentle.
Grow toward the sun; walk toward the light.
Keep going—frontiers love steady feet.
Nothing worth having comes easy.
Small steps still count as travel.
Today is a good day to begin again.
Be the calm in someone else’s weather.
Send a forecast of kindness.
The best jacket is a good attitude.
Clouds are temporary tenants of the sky.
Rainbows need both rain and light.
Even drizzle deserves a smile.
Make tea. Watch the window. Be here.
Your pace can match the weather.
Clear skies favor clear priorities.
Grey days are for soft music and warm soup.
Let heat remind you to rest, not rush.
Frost writes fine letters on glass.
Dew is the morning’s quiet jewelry.
Lightning is loud geometry.
Hail is winter visiting summer briefly.
Mist turns streets into watercolor.
Dust after wind means the air is resetting.
Humidity is invisible weight—drink water.
UV can hide behind thin clouds; protect your skin.
Windchill is why “feels like” matters.
Pressure drops can make joints complain—be gentle.
Urban nights stay warmer—city heat islands are real.
The coldest hour is often near dawn.
Peak heat usually arrives after noon, not at noon.
Blue skies come from scattered sunlight.
Red sunsets travel through thicker air.
Fog is a cloud that chose the ground.
Snowflakes love six-fold symmetry.
Thunder arrives late because sound is slower than light.
A 30% chance of rain is a probability, not a fraction of the day.
Radar shows echoes aloft; ground truth still matters.
Satellite “white” is often cloud tops reflecting sun.
Dress for the feel, not only the number.
Drive slower on wet roads—water lengthens braking.
Sip water in dry air; your lips will thank you.
Sunglasses help on bright days and snow glare.
If winter comes, can spring be far behind? — Percy Shelley
The best way out is always through. — Robert Frost
Keep your face always toward the sunshine. — Helen Keller
Even the darkest night will end and the sun will rise. — Victor Hugo
The journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step. — Lao Tzu
It always seems impossible until it’s done. — Nelson Mandela
What lies behind us and what lies before us are tiny matters compared to what lies within us. — Emerson
In the middle of difficulty lies opportunity. — Albert Einstein
Do what you can, with what you have, where you are. — Theodore Roosevelt
Happiness depends upon ourselves. — Aristotle
The only way to do great work is to love what you do. — Steve Jobs
Be yourself; everyone else is already taken. — Oscar Wilde
Not all those who wander are lost. — J. R. R. Tolkien
That which does not kill us makes us stronger. — Nietzsche
We are what we repeatedly do. — Will Durant (on Aristotle)
Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication. — Leonardo da Vinci
Time you enjoy wasting is not wasted time. — Bertrand Russell
An investment in knowledge pays the best interest. — Benjamin Franklin
Well begun is half done. — Aristotle
Fortune favors the bold.
Slow and steady wins the race.
Hope is a good breakfast.
Courage is fear that has said its prayers.
Grace under pressure.
Stay curious. Stay kind.
Ship the care. Share the sky.
Ride the wind and break the waves. — Li Bai
When one path fades, another village blooms. — Lu You
The moon waxes and wanes; so do our days. — Su Shi
Walk until the water ends; sit and watch clouds rise. — Wang Wei
A little rain knows the season. — Du Fu
Spring wind feels like scissors trimming the world green. — He Zhizhang
Stars don’t quiz travelers; time still rewards them.
With a calm heart, fear less of tomorrow.
Life isn’t about waiting for the storm to pass, but learning to dance in the rain.
May your inbox hold more clear skies.
Send this card like a hello through the weather.
You are allowed to rest until the rain softens.
The street smells new after rain—so can a day.
Clouds can’t cancel your plans forever.
Let the breeze say: you’ve got this.
Sunshine is free vitamin D—take a minute.
Rain sound is nature’s white noise.
In fog, focus on the next step.
In snow, leave romance to your eyes and care to your feet.
In heatwaves, hydrate more than you hustle.
When cold air arrives, check on family.
Forecasts change; keep your kindness constant.
Today suits deep breaths and warm soup.
Today suits looking up at clouds and down at the path.
Today suits a quiet smile to yourself.
Weather is vast; being human is enough.
Seasons turn, and so do you—growing.
This temperature is perfect for a kind thought.
Make today the weather you wanted.
Bear says: check the sky, keep the sunshine inside.
Bear says: walk slow in rain, jog light in sun.
Bear says: hat for wind, layers for cold.
Bear says: stay cozy and curious.
